note: D -- rules with at least one mutation observed provoking them. May rise, never fall. The entries are in enforce/discrimination.py and are meant to be read; the count alone says nothing about whether they are good.
why: Phase 2: D 15 -> 19. Four entries added after eight checks were narrowed to what they actually emit. ALLOC-002, ALLOC-004 and TEAMS-002 each get their own mutation because dispatch_recorded carries five claims and one entry would leave four resting on the other's evidence; each tree carries a filled allocation mapping so ALLOC-010 cannot fire alongside. FLOW-002's first draft was wrong -- it hit oracle_declared's TEST-004 path, and the rule fires on an oracle that is STATED and names none of the five.
